newsitem.title: GERMANY: Early German barley yields vary, high in southwest.
newsitem.headline: Early German barley yields vary, high in southwest.

text.p: Barley harvesting in Germany's southwest has produced winter grain yields of between 6.0 and 6.5 tonnes per hectare, grain trade paper Ernaehrungsdienst (ED) said on Monday.
The average national yield in 1996 was 5.61 tonnes.
Hectolitre weights in the area around Worms on the Upper Rhine, where the yields were measured, were 61-69 kilos, ED said.
Local feed plants were offering 220-225 marks/tonne for the barley free mill.
The states of Rhineland-Palatinate and North-Rhine Westphalia are expected to step up their harvesting efforts this week.
Neighbouring Dutch compound feed plants were reportedly not interested in buying newly harvested German barley.
In former eastern Germany, the states of Saxony and Thuringia were also beginning their barley harvest, with hectolitre weights only average at around 60 kilos.
Barley farmgate buyers across the country were quoting a wide 195-225 marks range for freshly cut material.
Exporters said new crop July/Aug barley free Baltic sea port was priced at 235 marks.
The German wheat harvest is still about a month away.
